resolvedQuestions.text: Which pre-write model check, rule set or validator does each corpus skill define before a FigJam write, and which of those rules are machine-enforced rather than advisory?

Which write route does each corpus skill use (hosted MCP `generate_diagram`, `use_figma` plugin API, console bridge, direct `fj`-style node script), and what read-back or verification follows the write?
How do the corpus skills handle FigJam's single implicit page, file creation, `fileKey` reuse and rollback, and what does that imply for Flow Mode's new-page rule?
How do the corpus skills handle Mermaid label and identifier hazards: emojis, reserved node IDs `end`/`subgraph`/`graph`, underscores in node IDs, and line breaks or markup?

Which layout, colour, shape, density and label limits does the corpus treat as enforceable versus advisory, and do they support or contradict Flow Mode's limits (TD only, 9 nodes, 3 decision exits, one accent colour, four shapes)?

keyFindings.text: Figma requires the `figma-generate-diagram` skill to be loaded before **every** `generate_diagram` call, because skipping it "causes preventable rendering failures and low-quality output"; the tool accepts Mermaid and returns an editable FigJam diagram [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:8]. Flow Mode has no equivalent pre-load requirement: its guard is the standalone `flow_check.py`, which knows only the Mermaid model, not the tool schema or its failure modes [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:62].

Official colour guidance permits multiple semantic colours — status, ownership, subsystem — as long as colour encodes meaning and not every node is painted [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:267] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:282]. Flow Mode's one-accent rule is stricter than the vendor and is enforced by counting distinct hex values in `style`/`classDef`/`linkStyle` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:47].

Emojis are a hard tool-level rejection, stated as universal constraint #1 and repeated in the label audit: "No emojis (tool rejects)" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:49] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:318]. Flow Mode's check has no emoji rule at all: `MARKUP_MARKS` lists only `<`, `>`, newline, `**` and backtick, so an emoji-bearing label passes [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:44]. This is a confirmed Flow Mode gap, not a hypothetical.

Reserved node IDs are named explicitly — `end`, `subgraph`, `graph` — and node IDs must be camelCase with no spaces because "underscores can break edge routing in some processors" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:52] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:53]. The same pair is repeated in the flowchart reference [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:321]. `flow_check.py` never inspects node IDs — it validates shape, direction, label markup, decision exits and node count only — so `end`, `subgraph`, `graph` and underscore IDs pass the pre-write gate [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:57].

FigJam has one implicit page, and `figma.createPage()` throws `TypeError: figma.createPage no such property 'createPage' on the figma global object`; the official guidance is to organize with FigJam sections instead [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md:13]. The same warning is carried in the generate-diagram constraints for hybrid `use_figma` extensions [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:57]. Flow Mode's gate nevertheless offers "a new page, or a page you have read and found empty" as the target and defines rollback as "clearing the page" [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:115] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:117]. For a FigJam board created by `generate_diagram`, that page premise is unsatisfiable: there is no page to create and nothing to clear.

`generate_diagram` creates its own file: calling `create_new_file` first is explicitly forbidden, and every call without a `fileKey` creates a new draft file [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:92] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:102]. Flow Mode's gate asks the operator to state "the target plan, file and page" before the write [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:63], which presumes the operator supplies a file that the hosted route would only create.

Official iteration policy is `fileKey` reuse plus deliberate deletion: pass the existing board's `fileKey` for follow-ups, and to replace rather than add, delete the old diagram's nodes through `use_figma` before regenerating [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:109] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:110]. Flow Mode has no `fileKey` guidance, no reuse rule and no delete-before-regenerate recipe; its recovery says re-run into a cleared page only after user agreement [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:159].

Direction: the official default is `flowchart LR`, with `TD`/`TB` reserved for hierarchies, taxonomies, deep narrow trees or many siblings at one level [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:26] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:27]. Flow Mode makes TD mandatory for every diagram [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:41]. The official guidance therefore supports TD as a valid choice but not as the only choice.

Density: official soft caps are ~20 nodes fine, 20–30 consider subgraphs, 30+ split; the validation checklist uses "≤ ~25 nodes" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:329] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:349]. Flow Mode caps at 9 nodes and requires splitting a longer flow [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:99]. Flow Mode is 2.2–2.8× stricter than the vendor's own soft cap.

Official validation is a prose checklist of eight human judgements (cycle check, orphans, input/output, label audit, shape audit, colour audit, subgraph audit, density check) with no executable checker [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:337]. Flow Mode is the outlier in the good direction: it is the only source so far with a machine-enforced gate and planted-failure self-test [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:154].

Widened corpus: `parse-figjam` is a read-back-only skill that extracts semantic context from FigJam board JSON produced by the Figma REST API, with no write route at all [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:8]. It fills the one role every pinned source treats as secondary — reading a board as data rather than as a picture.

Limit verdict — **3 exits per decision: keep unchanged**. The official guidance treats 2–3 level decision trees as the normal case, rocket-path's decision trees use three labelled exits, and no source allows a fourth without splitting [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:26] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/references/examples.md:92]. Flow Mode's rule is the corpus's clearest enforceable contribution.

Limit verdict — **one accent colour: change the unit from hex to accent family**. The official guidance allows multiple semantic colours for status, ownership and subsystem; IamTheLime keeps one accent plus note and warning roles; FMCP keeps a per-lane semantic palette [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:267] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/themes.md:26]. Counting distinct hexes rejects a disciplined palette; counting accent families preserves the intent.

Limit verdict — **four shapes: keep, and cite the vendor table as justification**. The official table lists rectangle, stadium, circle (rendered as an ellipse) and diamond as distinct rendered shapes, so all four Flow Mode shapes are vendor-validated, while most other Mermaid shapes fall back to rectangles [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:35] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:41]. rocket-path's "full range" claim is the counterexample that proves the limit's value [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:52].

The new source also exposes a round-trip Flow Mode lacks: it can emit Mermaid from a board as one of six output choices [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:112]. Flow Mode only goes model → board, so revising an existing board from its model is impossible without retyping the model.

The read is deliberately semantic: it extracts `name`, `characters`, `type` and `children`, and ignores fifteen layout and appearance fields including `absoluteBoundingBox`, `size`, `cornerRadius`, `shapeType` and `effects` [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:31] [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:62]. Flow Mode's read-back compares counts and labels from a screenshot; a REST semantic read is cheaper, deterministic and searchable, and would make the "missing label" list iteration 9 asked for trivial to produce [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65].

Connector direction is derived from the caps, not from the model's order: one arrow means directed, both arrows bidirectional, none undirected [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:50]. Flow Mode's read-back counts connectors and labels but never checks whether an arrow points the way the model said [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65]. This is a confirmed verification gap.

A dashed line is a distinct relationship type, not styling: `strokeDashes` present means dashed, absent means solid, and the relationship is reported with its line style [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:48] [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:102]. Flow Mode has no dashed/solid semantic and its one-accent rule cannot express one [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:47].

Colour meaning is not assumed: if a section named `legend` exists its contents map colours to meanings, and without one and with significant variation the skill asks the user [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:57] [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:58]. Flow Mode's single accent is self-explanatory (happy path), but there is no legend convention on multi-diagram boards, which iteration 9 also flagged [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:102].

Unknown content is surfaced, never skipped: a missing endpoint becomes `"external reference to [nodeId]"`, an unknown node type is included with its raw type name, and an empty section is noted rather than omitted [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:144] [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:145]. Flow Mode's read-back has no unknown-item category, so an unexpected node is neither reported nor counted.

The full JSON tree is never reproduced in output [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:146], corroborating iterations 2, 3, 6 and 7 on bounded reads and returning only what the comparison needs.

Limit verdict — **TD only: keep as house style, reject as a rule**. No corpus source mandates top-to-bottom. The official default is LR; rocket-path uses LR with TD only for decision trees; ompug's linter accepts five directions; Mermaid Jam accepts five [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:26] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:211]. The rule should become "TD is the default for user flows; a linear hand-off may use LR", and `flow_check.py` should accept both.

Limit verdict — **9 nodes: keep, with a naming obligation**. The official soft cap is ~20, ompug's is ~25, FMCP times out at 7–12 nodes per call, and rocket-path's densest worked example is exactly 9 [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:329] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/references/diagram-types.md:31] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/references/examples.md:22]. Nine is defensible for board reading and matches the only practitioner example at that size. What is missing is ompug's rule that anything omitted in a split is named, never dropped silently [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/references/diagram-types.md:32].

**Emoji rule** — add an emoji error to `sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py` (the `MARKUP_MARKS` tuple at line 44 and `diagram_problems`), sourced from the official universal constraint and ompug's line-level emoji error [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:49] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:151]. It is the cheapest fix in the set and closes a tool-level rejection.

keyFindings.text: **"Accent family" is not implementable as written.** A family needs a membership rule — hue distance, a named palette, or a role map — and Flow Mode has none of the three. Any threshold would be arbitrary and untestable, so iteration 10's recommendation is withdrawn: the check stays at one hex until a palette exists [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:45] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/themes.md:26]. This is the iteration's main correction.

**Every new rule needs its own planted model.** `self_test` proves each rule fails on a planted case and the good model passes; adding a check without a `PLANTED` entry silently weakens the suite [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:119] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:160]. The four needed models are an emoji label, a reserved-ID node, an underscore ID and an 81-character label; the subgraph rejection needs a fifth with `subgraph`/`end`.

**The existing `GOOD` model survives all five additions.** It uses four nodes, short labels, no emoji, camelCase IDs and one accent, so the new checks do not require rewriting the passing fixture [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:109]. That keeps the change additive.

**The underscore rule must not fire on edge labels.** Flow Mode edges are unlabelled by ID; only node IDs are identifiers. Applying the rule to the edge's label text would reject ordinary prose with underscores, so the check belongs in the node loop only [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:63].

**One hex remains the right unit for a nine-node flow.** Colour in Flow Mode marks the happy path or one decision, and the model carries no role vocabulary for note or warning. Counting hexes is exact, self-testable and matches the product rule; counting families would be a new spec with a new failure mode [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:88]. If a palette is ever added, it belongs in `flow-templates.md` and the check should count roles, not hexes.

**Subgraph verdict: reject explicitly.** Three independent reasons converge. At nine nodes a subgraph grouping is rarely worth its visual weight, the official guidance itself says not to subgraph a pair and to reserve subgraphs for 3+ related nodes; the official subgraph recipe requires per-subgraph tint fills, which collide with the one-accent rule; and it advertises per-subgraph direction overrides, which collide with the TD-only rule [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:146] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:169]. Mermaid Jam's rejection supplies the precedent [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:23].

**Supporting subgraphs would cascade into three rule changes, not one.** The official guidance couples subgraphs to tinted fills, per-subgraph direction and node-to-node edges rather than subgraph-to-subgraph edges [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:153] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:157]. Adopting it would mean relaxing the accent rule, the direction rule and the connector rule at once — a product redesign, not a fix. Rejection is the smaller, more coherent choice.

**The four mechanical checks fit the checker's existing shape.** Each is a constant plus a condition inside `diagram_problems`, exactly like `MARKUP_MARKS` and `MAX_NODES` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:40] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:57]. No new dependency is needed: node IDs and labels are already on `diagram.nodes`, and `block_text` is already passed for the accent check.

**The subgraph check must read `block_text`, like the accent check.** The extractor drops styling lines, so the raw block is the only reliable place to spot a `subgraph` keyword and its closing `end` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:46]. A regex anchored at line start is enough; it does not need to parse nesting.

**The reserved-ID check needs whole-word, case-insensitive matching.** `end` must trip `end`, `endNode` and `END`, but not `ending` or `weekend`. Mermaid keywords are lowercase and reserved in node position, so the match should be on the node ID token, not a substring [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:37].

**The emoji check should scan labels and edge labels together.** `MARKUP_MARKS` is applied to both today, and an emoji in a decision exit label breaks the same way as one in a node [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:66] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:78]. A single emoji range test in one helper keeps the two paths consistent.

**Label length should be a hard error at 80 characters.** ompug truncates at 80 and Mermaid Jam simplifies at 120; for nine-node diagrams read on a board, 80 is the readable bound, and a hard error is testable where a warning is not [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:25] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/shared/reviser.ts:138]. The rule should count characters after trimming, not bytes.

**Every proposed check has its data already.** `Node` exposes `id`, `label`, `shape`; `Edge` exposes `source`, `target`, `label`, `style`, `arrowhead`, `bidirectional`, `undirected` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:63] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:79]. The reserved-ID, underscore, emoji and length rules are conditions on fields that already exist; none needs a parser change.

**The extractor's limits do not shadow the checker's.** `MAX_NODES = 2000` and `MAX_EDGES = 5000` sit far above Flow Mode's 9, so a ten-node model parses and then fails the checker's rule; the existing planted test is reachable [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:36] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:75]. Had the extractor capped at 9, the checker's test would have exited 2 instead of 1.

**The subgraph scan must be anchored to a statement start.** A label such as `Enter subgraph settings` contains the word but is not a subgraph; anchoring `^\s*subgraph\b` on the raw block avoids the false positive, matching the accent check's anchored-regex style [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:47].

**The edge rule and the board read-back can share one vocabulary.** Model-side `style` and `arrowhead` map directly onto `parse-figjam`'s `strokeDashes` and cap fields, so the checker's error names the same property the read-back inspects [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:42] [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:48]. That makes the new rule the first Flow Mode rule with an exact inverse check.

**New gap: `flow_check.py` never validates edge operators.** A probe of `-.->`, `---`, `<-->` and `==>` produced `style=dashed`, `undirected=True`, `bidirectional=True` and `style=thick` respectively, and all four pass the checker because it only looks at edge labels [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:77] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:181]. Flow Mode's model is therefore allowed to contain an undirected connector, a two-way connector, a dashed relationship or a thick edge — four semantics the board will faithfully render and the read-back has no vocabulary to reject.

**The edge rule should be: solid, one-directional, arrow at the target.** That is the only operator set consistent with a flow whose connectors mean "then". `---` yields a connector with no arrowhead, which `parse-figjam` would read as undirected [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:50]; `<-->` yields two arrowheads, read as bidirectional. Both contradict a directed user flow and neither is caught today.

**Two of the five markup marks are dead conditions.** `clean_label` strips `<...>` tags and `**`/`__` emphasis before the checker sees a label, so the `<`, `>` and `**` entries in `MARKUP_MARKS` can never match a `node.label` or `edge.label` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:234] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:44]. A probe confirmed `Use **bold** and tag` arrives as `Use bold and tag`.

**Only the line-break mark survives cleaning.** `
` becomes a real newline and the cleaned label keeps it, so `\n` still fires — which is why the planted line-break test passes and hides the dead marks [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:139]. The rule's guarantee is narrower than its docstring claims: it rejects line breaks, not markup.

**The raw text still carries markup to the generator.** The extractor is a checker-side reader; the Mermaid block sent to `generate_diagram` is the original text. So a model with `**bold**` passes the check and the generator silently drops the markup, producing plain text rather than a rejected model. The rule should either scan `block_text` (as the accent check already does) or be reworded to cover line breaks only [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:46].

**Backticks are stripped only when they wrap the whole label**, so the backtick mark is dead for the common case and would fire only for an interior backtick [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:239]. A raw-text scan resolves all three dead marks in one change.

**Emoji survives cleaning**, so the emoji rule can run on `node.label` and `edge.label` directly; the probe kept `Start ✅` and `Yes 👍` intact [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:249]. No raw-text scan is needed for emoji.

**Node IDs are never cleaned**, so the reserved-word and underscore rules can test `node.id` exactly as written; `_strip_class_suffix` removes only a `:::class` attachment [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:569]. A reserved word in a label is harmless; only an ID matters.

**The rule list grows from seven bullets to nine, and the split sentence must change with it.** Current order is shapes, exits, nodes, direction, labels, accent, generator; the check owns the first six and the read-back owns the last [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:95]. Inserting edges after direction and subgraphs after edges gives nine bullets, the check owning the first eight and the read-back the last [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:97]. Leaving the sentence at "first six" would silently misdescribe the gate.

**Eight planted models prove the new rules.** Emoji label, reserved `end` ID, underscore ID, 81-character label, an undirected `---` edge, a dashed `-.->` edge, a `subgraph` block and an HTML-tag label; each must exit 1 [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:119]. Without them the self-test proves only the old six rules, and a regression in any new condition would pass unnoticed.

**The good fixture and all five shipped patterns survive.** `GOOD` uses camelCase IDs, short labels, one accent and solid arrows; the longest label in `flow-templates.md` is 27 characters and none of the patterns uses a dashed edge, an underscore or a subgraph [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:109] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/flow-templates.md:39]. The change is additive at both sites.

**The rule wording should fold length and emoji into the existing label bullet.** Replace "Labels are one plain line" with "Labels are one plain line of at most 80 characters, with no HTML tag, emphasis markup or emoji", which keeps nine bullets rather than growing eleven and puts all label constraints in one place [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:101]. The edge and subgraph bullets are new; length and emoji are not.

**The check's docstring needs the same edit as the rule list.** It enumerates the rules today, so a new edge rule that is absent from the docstring makes `--help` and the self-test describe different contracts [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:16]. Update both in the same change or the docstring becomes the next stale mirror.

**Proposed constants** — add `MAX_LABEL = 80`, `EMOJI = re.compile("[\U0001F300-\U0001FAFF\u2600-\u27BF]")`, `RESERVED_IDS = {"end", "subgraph", "graph", "flowchart"}`, `SUBGRAPH = re.compile(r"^\s*subgraph\b", re.I | re.M)` and `HTML_TAG = re.compile(r"<[A-Za-z/][^>]*>")` beside the existing block [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:40]. The reserved set stays small because only keywords that break parsing belong there; Mermaid's wider keyword list is a linter concern, not a gate concern [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:37].

**Reserved IDs should be matched exactly, not case-insensitively.** Mermaid keywords are lowercase and IDs are case-sensitive, so `End` is a legal ID while `end` is not; iteration 12's whole-word, case-insensitive suggestion would reject a legal model [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:63]. Membership in a set is simpler than a regex and has no false positives.

**Edge condition** — inside the existing edge loop: reject `edge.style != "solid"`, `edge.undirected` and `edge.bidirectional`, with one message naming the operator's meaning, for example `edge a to b is undirected; Flow Mode connectors are solid and one-way` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:77]. The probe confirmed the three fields carry exactly these states for `---`, `<-->`, `-.->` and `==>` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/vendored/mermaid_extract.py:181].

**The raw markup scan must not look for a bare `<` or `>`.** `>` occurs in every `-->` operator and `<` in `<-->`, so a naive scan would flag the whole model. Match an HTML tag (`<[A-Za-z/][^>]*>`) and `**` instead, and keep the newline check on the cleaned label [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:46]. This is the precise correction to iteration 13's "scan raw text" recommendation.

**Emoji check belongs on the cleaned labels.** One condition in the node loop and one in the edge loop, both using the same regex, since a decision-exit label renders the same way as a node label [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:66] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:78]. The probe showed emoji survive `clean_label` untouched.

**Label length should be measured after cleaning.** The cleaned label is what renders, so `len(node.label) > MAX_LABEL` is the honest test; measuring the raw source would count markup the board never shows [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:63]. One condition, shared by node and edge labels.

**Underscore stays an error and camelCase stays unenforced.** `"_" in node.id` is exact and testable; a camelCase warning would need a second output channel and a non-binary exit code the checker does not have [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:83]. Deferring the warning keeps the gate's contract: exit 0 passes, 1 fails, 2 unreadable.

**Subgraph rejection is a raw-text condition, not a node condition.** `SUBGRAPH.search(block_text)` reports `subgraph blocks are not supported; split the diagram at a hand-off` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:57]. Anchoring at line start avoids a label that merely contains the word, and the check does not need to count nesting because every subgraph is rejected.

**The page rule is seven statements across three files, not one.** `flow-mode.md` carries it at the gate, the write bullet and the rollback; the mirror repeats all three; the kernel compresses it into the Flow Mode Delivery line [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:63] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:115] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:117] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/knowledge/Product Owner - Templates - Flow Mode.md:41] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/knowledge/Product Owner - Templates - Flow Mode.md:93] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/knowledge/Product Owner - Templates - Flow Mode.md:95] [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/claude project/Custom Instructions.md:249]. A fix that edits one surface leaves six live statements of a rule the vendor API forbids.

keyFindings.text: **Emoji range corrected.** The proposed `\u2600-\u27BF` range misses pictographs above it and includes nothing above the BMP; ompug's published regex covers `1F000–1FAFF`, `1FC00–1FFFD`, `☀–➿`, `⌀–⏿` and `⬀–⯿` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/sanitize.py:173]. Adopt that range verbatim rather than inventing a narrower one; a checkmark `✓` sits inside `☀–➿` and is rejected, which matches the sanitizer this corpus already runs [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/sanitize.py:310].

**Section idempotency is by name, which the read-back can use.** Ompug's placement reuses a section already tagged with the same diagram and recognises its sections by name [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/scripts.py:12]. Flow Mode's `Read-back:` line can name the section and count only its children, which is the v2 format from iteration 16.
**The edge rule survives all four attacks.** No corpus source uses an undirected or dashed edge in a flowchart that Flow Mode targets, and the named alternatives cover the intents. Its rank stays 1.

**The table's top five are now: edge rule, section/file rule, `fileKey` reuse, emoji, reserved IDs.** Underscore moves to six. The shift is not cosmetic: it puts the two write-route fixes above three mechanical checks, because the write-route failures lose work while the checks only lose a call [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:117].

**Reserved-ID case handling corrected to case-insensitive.** ompug lowercases the ID before comparing it against both sets [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:520]. Iteration 14's exact-match advice is withdrawn: the cost is rejecting `End`, an ID no Flow Mode diagram needs, and the benefit is matching the only linter in the corpus.

**Attack on the edge rule: thick edges are stylistic, not semantic.** `==>` changes stroke weight, not direction, so a thick edge does not break the flow's meaning. It should still be rejected, but for a different reason: Flow Mode already has one emphasis channel, colour, and a second one makes two ways to say "important" [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:102]. The error message should say that, or the rule reads as arbitrary.

**Attack on the edge rule: dashed and undirected edges have legitimate uses elsewhere.** A dashed edge often means "later" or "optional", and an undirected edge means a plain association; both are meaningful in other diagram types. In Flow Mode they are not needed because a label carries "later" and a loop back with `-->` carries repetition [SOURCE: https://github.com/rrichardsonv/parse-figjam/blob/HEAD/SKILL.md:48]. The rule stands, with a named alternative in the message so a user is not left without a way to express the intent.

**Attack on the section rule: it collides with "the generator owns the layout".** `generate_diagram` without a `fileKey` creates a new file in drafts, and adding to an existing file places the diagram beside the old one; section placement is a separate `use_figma` step that reparents nodes [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:102] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:110]. Reparenting is a move, and Flow Mode forbids moving generated nodes. The two rules cannot both stand unqualified.

**Resolution: scope the never-move rule, do not drop containment.** Allow exactly one post-write move — reparenting the diagram into a named section without changing its relative geometry — and keep the ban on rearranging nodes or rewiring connectors. Ompug's placement script exists for this purpose and handles parent/local coordinates [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/scripts.py:103]. On a route with no section step, the diagram lives in its own file and containment is satisfied by the file.

**The page rule's replacement gets simpler, not harder.** There is no page to name: the target is a file (new, or existing by `fileKey`) and optionally a section. The gate's effect becomes "a new file, or N nodes added to an existing file"; the rollback becomes "delete the created nodes or section". That removes the impossible page choice entirely instead of substituting another page-shaped rule [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:109].

**`fileKey` reuse is under-ranked at 10.** Without it, every regeneration creates a draft file; the official guidance counts four regenerations as four files to clean up [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:102]. Reuse is also the mechanism that makes revision possible at all, so it moves to rank 3, ahead of the three ID rules, and the page-rule row merges into it.

**Deleting the old diagram before regenerating is the official replacement recipe.** It is the rollback path, not a page clear: delete the previous diagram's nodes via `use_figma`, then regenerate with the same `fileKey` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:110]. Flow Mode's recovery section should adopt that sentence instead of "re-run into a cleared page".

The skill's stated verification is visual and mandatory: "Verify with `get_screenshot` before declaring anything finished", because "overlaps are invisible until you look" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:12]. Flow Mode's read-back does require a screenshot check for stretched or overlapping connectors [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65], so the rule agrees; what IamTheLime adds is a named tool and a pre-declaration gate rather than a step in a prose list.

Read-back needs a bounded inspection strategy: `get_figjam` on a whole page can exceed the response limit and fail to parse, so query a node or return a filtered summary; `get_metadata` is design-file only; `get_screenshot` needs a real `nodeId` and section ids are the useful ones [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/api-notes.md:9] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/api-notes.md:14]. Flow Mode's read-back does not name an inspection tool or a bounded query [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65], so this is a concrete adoptable recipe.

Branches can be distinguished without colour by `connectorEndStrokeCap` (`ARROW_LINES`, `ARROW_EQUILATERAL`, `TRIANGLE_FILLED`, `DIAMOND_FILLED`, `CIRCLE_FILLED`, `NONE`), which survives greyscale and colour blindness [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/api-notes.md:78] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:166]. Flow Mode's one-accent rule creates the same risk; this is a route-compatible alternative on `fj`, and a reader-accessibility argument the hosted route cannot express.

Tables are their own primitive: `figma.createTable()` for genuinely tabular content, not a grid of shapes, and tables have no strokes [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:192] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/api-notes.md:89]. Flow Mode has no comparison-table pattern, and its four-shape rule would force a shape grid if a flow comparison were requested [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/flow-templates.md:39].

`figma.createPage()` does not exist in FigJam, **but boards can have several pages**: `figma.root.children` lists them and `figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` switches [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/api-notes.md:18] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/api-notes.md:20]. This refines iteration 1 finding 4: the impossibility is page **creation**, not page existence. Flow Mode's new-page rule is unachievable from a plugin, but a pre-existing empty page could be selected through the page API; the honest fix is to drop page creation and keep "read the target before writing".

Structure replaces pages: "Nothing lives loose on the canvas" and "`page.children` should contain exactly one section" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:122] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:129]. This is a directly adoptable replacement for Flow Mode's page-based rollback: one board section per diagram gives a deletable, addressable unit that is not a page [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:117].

The palette rule is "one MAIN colour carries all emphasis; everything else stays quiet", and explicitly forbids a second accent family [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:19] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:23]. It nevertheless keeps note (`#c2e5ff`) and warning (`#ff6655`) roles alongside `MAIN` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/themes.md:26]. Flow Mode's checker counts **distinct hex values** and permits one, so this palette would fail Flow Mode even though it obeys "one accent" [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:51]. The rule to adopt is "one accent family", not "one hex".

Text belongs in text nodes, never in a shape's built-in text, because shape text "cannot be styled per run, it centres by default, its wrapping is not yours to control" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:79] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:81]. This is only actionable on the `fj`/`use_figma` route; `generate_diagram` owns its node text. It is a `fj`-route quality rule Flow Mode lacks [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:123].

Shape vocabulary is deliberately smaller and sharper than Flow Mode's four: `SQUARE` (never `ROUNDED_RECTANGLE`), `DIAMOND` for a decision, dashed border for commentary or a superseded state, and borderless for ordinary boxes [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:152] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:156] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:159]. It has no stadium and no merge-dot circle, so adopting it wholesale would delete two of Flow Mode's four shapes [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:97]. The transferable part is the **information-bearing border** (bright = standout, dashed = commentary), not the shape list.

Deleting a node silently deletes its connectors, so after any removal the skill requires re-listing connectors and confirming every decision still has all its branches [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:188]. This is the missing caution on the official fileKey-replacement recipe from iteration 1 finding 6, which says to delete the old diagram's nodes before regenerating without warning that the delete cascades [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md:110].

Connector labels sit at the line midpoint with no offset control, and "long connector labels collide with boxes"; the skill's fix is a few words on the connector and detail in a box [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:117] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/references/api-notes.md:81]. Flow Mode's one-plain-line label rule gives the generator as the reason [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:101]; IamTheLime gives the geometric reason, which survives a route switch.

The density numbers are spatial and route-dependent: 20–24px box padding, 30px between boxes in a row, 120–160px between bands, 60px section padding, and one fixed flow-box size reused throughout [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:106] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/IamTheLime__dotfiles/agents/skills/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:110]. Flow Mode has no spacing guidance at all because the hosted generator owns layout [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:103]; these numbers are only adoptable on the `fj` route, where Flow Mode computes every position.

**The final set is thirteen changes, twelve ranked and one route-specific batch.** The ranking changed twice under scrutiny: `fileKey` rose from ten to three, and the page rule fell from two to a file-level rule inside rank 2 [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:115]. The synthesis should publish the final order, not iteration 11's first draft.

keyFindings.text: **The strongest single finding of the research is the page rule.** It is the only Flow Mode instruction that is impossible on the vendor API and destructive on a shared board, and it appears in eight statements across three files plus two recovery sections [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md:13]. The second strongest is the unchecked edge operator, which silently produces undirected or reversed connectors [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:77].
