keyFindings.text: This skill positions itself as the granular alternative to the native one-shot `generate_diagram`, for "specific colors, positions, magnets, or to extend an existing board" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/SKILL.md:10]. Flow Mode has the same two-level split, but its granular level is `figma-ds-cli fj` rather than a console/Plugin API bridge [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:121]. The split is confirmed as a general pattern, not a Flow Mode quirk.

The route is Desktop-only because the Plugin API is unavailable in the browser [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/SKILL.md:40]. This matches Flow Mode's statement that `figma-ds-cli` writes into the FigJam file open in Figma Desktop [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:121], and reinforces that the hosted route is the only Desktop-free option.

Every operation starts with a file-kind guard: `return { editorType: figma.editorType };` must be `'figjam'`, because "every op throws outside FigJam" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/SKILL.md:24] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:5]. Flow Mode's `fj` route checks the daemon and version but not the file kind before the first write [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:121]. Adopt the guard.

The retry model is atomic: "atomic errors (a failed script applies nothing — read the error, fix, retry)" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/SKILL.md:18]. Flow Mode's recovery is page-oriented — re-run the write into a cleared page only after the user agrees, because a second write duplicates the board [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:159]. Atomicity is a stronger guarantee than rollback-by-clear, and it removes the need to renegotiate with the user after a failed call.

Connectors require real node IDs, so the workflow is create nodes first, capture their returned IDs, then create connectors referencing those IDs with start/end plus magnets [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/SKILL.md:28]. Flow Mode arrives at the same requirement from the other direction: read node ids back with `fj nodes -l` between steps when a create verb prints none [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:125]. Two independent sources make this a durable rule.

Read-back has two specialized queries, not one: "read board contents" returns a bounded node list (`MAX_NODES = 500`) with id, type, name, geometry, text, shapeType and per-type extras; "read the connection graph" returns every connector with `connectorStart`/`connectorEnd`, label, plus connected-node count [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:196] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:219]. Flow Mode's read-back compares node count, connector count and labels but has no query recipe and no edge endpoint check [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65].

The connection-graph read supplies exactly the evidence Flow Mode's read-back lacks: for each connector, which node is on each end and what the label says, so a connector attached to the wrong pair is detectable, not merely countable [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:221]. Counting connectors cannot distinguish a correct wiring from a permuted one.

The board read is deliberately bounded and type-filtered rather than a whole-page dump: it breaks at `MAX_NODES`, walks `figma.currentPage.children`, and records only FigJam types [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:197] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:200]. This corroborates iteration 2 finding 10's warning that a whole-page read can overflow, and gives a concrete shape for the bounded read.

Auto-arrange is a post-creation positioning helper: grid, horizontal or vertical layout with a configurable gap, computed from current node geometry [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:170] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/references/figjam-snippets.md:180]. Flow Mode's `fj` route computes every position by hand "because `fj` has no layout verb" [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:123]; an arrange pass would replace a large amount of that arithmetic, at the cost of a second write pass.

Fonts must be loaded before any text write, with an Inter fallback when the node's default font is unavailable [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/SKILL.md:31] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/southleft__figma-console-mcp-skills/skills/figjam-create-content/SKILL.md:32]. Flow Mode's `fj` route has no font rule, and no fallback if a font fails to load [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:124].

The write is staged: create **one** native pattern first, verify it with `get_screenshot`, `get_figjam` and a Labor read, then batch the remaining nodes, and finish with a screenshot of the created or changed root node [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:15] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:18]. Flow Mode's write is one shot — every diagram is sent per call and the board is read only after the whole write [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:114]. A one-node canary would catch a schema or colour failure before the remaining nodes are spent.

The route confirms the file-kind pre-flight requirement from iteration 3: confirm `figma.editorType === "figjam"` when it is unclear [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:13]. Two independent repos now require the guard, which makes it a corpus-level norm rather than one skill's habit.

A wrong mutation is undone immediately with `labor_undo`, not repaired in place [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:139]. Flow Mode's `fj` rollback is page duplication before the first write, then Undo in the session or restore from version history [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:127]. Per-mutation undo is finer-grained and does not depend on a pre-write snapshot being taken.

Verification has a structural checklist beyond visuals: text is present, connector endpoints are correct, table dimensions and cell indexes are correct, section visibility is correct, and no temporary nodes remain [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:127] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:133]. Flow Mode's read-back covers node count, connector count, labels and decision-exit labels only [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65]; endpoint correctness is not in it, which iteration 3 finding 6 also flagged.

Read-back has documented fallbacks: if `get_screenshot` is unavailable, use the image from `get_figjam` or `labor_zoom_to_node` for manual inspection [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:125]. Flow Mode's read-back assumes a screenshot exists and has no degraded path when it does not [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65].

Temporary test nodes are an explicit lifecycle concept: they are created for the canary and must be removed before completion [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:19] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:133]. Flow Mode has no scratch-node concept, so any probe shape it writes stays on the board and inflates the read-back counts.

Placement starts by scanning nearby top-level nodes before choosing coordinates, creating sections before their content, passing `parentId` when content belongs in a section, and avoiding reparenting finished nodes unless local coordinates are recalculated [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:36] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:39]. Flow Mode's `fj` route computes every position but has no "scan before placing" rule [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:123]; this is the same collision risk iteration 2 raised with sections.

Connector defaults are typed: `ELBOWED` for structure, straight connectors use `CENTER` or `NONE` magnets, elbowed and curved connectors usually use `AUTO`, and endpoints must be re-read after every reassignment [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:61] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:79]. Flow Mode's `fj connect` takes no label and no documented magnet or line-type policy [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:124]; on the hosted route the generator owns these choices.

Font ownership is explicit: dedicated text tools load required fonts, `labor_run_script` must load fonts before changing embedded text, new connector labels need a valid fallback font, and code blocks require Source Code Pro Medium [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:110] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:113]. This corroborates iteration 3 finding 9 with a second independent repo and adds a code-block-specific font requirement.

The capability limits are stated as product constraints, not style advice: components, variants, variables and design libraries are Design-only; widgets, stamps, highlights and embeds may be inspectable without being creatable [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:137] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/mkaralevich__pi-figma-labor/skills/figjam-create/SKILL.md:138]. Flow Mode's four-shape rule happens to stay inside the creatable set, but the skill does not state the boundary, so an operator asking for a widget or component would hit an undocumented wall [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:97].

This skill uses the same hosted route as Flow Mode — "the `generate_diagram` MCP tool, which converts Mermaid.js syntax into editable FigJam boards" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:8]. Same tool, so every difference below is a rule choice, not a route artefact.

It repeats the emoji prohibition as a general rule for every diagram type [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:41], a third independent confirmation of iteration 1 finding 2 and further evidence that `flow_check.py`'s missing emoji rule is a real defect [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:44].

Its iteration advice is only "start simple — generate a minimal diagram first, then iterate" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:151]; unlike iteration 4's canary, it attaches no verification to the minimal first diagram, so the iteration is unguarded.

Its delivery has **no read-back**: Step 4 is "The tool returns a FigJam link. Share it with the user" and suggests opening the board to edit [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:105]. Flow Mode's counted read-back is therefore not a corpus norm; it is a Flow Mode strength that the closest competitor lacks [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:140].

It quotes **every** shape and edge label by default: `A["Start"]`, `A -->|"Yes"| B` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:48] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:51]. The official skill quotes only labels with special characters [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:323], and Flow Mode's templates are unquoted [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/flow-templates.md:45]. Universal quoting is the safe superset: it satisfies the official special-character rule without changing rendered text.

It advertises the "full range of shapes" — rect, rounded, diamond, stadium, subroutine, circle, flag, hexagon [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:52]. This contradicts the official warning that "most silently fall back to a plain rectangle in FigJam" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:33]. Flow Mode's four-shape rule is closer to the documented renderer behaviour; this repo's permissiveness is a trap, not a capability.

It defaults to `LR` and uses `TD` only for decision trees [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:47]. Combined with iteration 1's official default, that is **three** independent sources preferring LR for process flows. Flow Mode's TD-only rule is a deliberate house style, not a corpus norm, and should be documented as such rather than justified as a generator requirement [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:62].

Its only validation is post-hoc: "the `generate_diagram` tool will reject invalid syntax" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:38]. This is the second corpus source (after official Figma's prose checklist, iteration 1) with no pre-write model gate, deepening iteration 1 finding 9: Flow Mode's executable `flow_check.py` is the outlier in the good direction.

It reserves `end` for state-diagram class names [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:79], corroborating the reserved-word hazard in a **second** diagram type and strengthening the case for a node-ID check in `flow_check.py` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:44].

It recommends subgraphs for complex flowcharts (`subgraph "Section Name"`) and its examples use quoted subgraph names [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:152] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/references/examples.md:51]. Flow Mode has no subgraph policy at all — it neither uses nor forbids them — while the official reference supports them at up to two levels of nesting [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:157].

Its densest worked example is a **9-node** `flowchart LR` onboarding flow, and its decision trees use three labelled exits [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/references/examples.md:22] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/references/examples.md:92]. That is empirical support for Flow Mode's 9-node and 3-exit caps from a practitioner who never adopted them — the limits match what a hand-authored example library actually draws.

The skill exists to stop tool results from breaking the session: it mandates short returns — `"OK: 12 node, 14 connector"`, errors capped near 200 characters, small JSON — and forbids returning big node lists, `currentPage.children` or pluginData dumps [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:49] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:53]. Flow Mode has no response-size budget for its read-back, and iteration 2 already warned that a whole-page read can overflow [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65].

The skill carries evolution triggers — if the bridge adds FigJam-specific tools, or the payload limit changes, or new diagram types are requested, the strategy must be revised [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:178] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:180]. Flow Mode has no stated trigger that would tell a maintainer when its route assumptions have expired.

Swimlanes are a first-class pattern with a per-lane semantic palette and dashed connectors for alternative flow [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:110] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:115]. Flow Mode's TD-only, four-shape model cannot express lanes at all, so any cross-role flow is forced into a linear chain [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:100].

Coordinates are never persisted between steps; they are recomputed every step from one constant table (`OX=3500, OY=100, LW=160, CW=300, LH=200, HH=64, NW=240, NH=76`) so a retry lands in the same place [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:72] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:77]. Flow Mode's `fj` route computes every position but specifies no constant table [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:123]; without one, two runs of the same model can produce different layouts.

Production is split into three phases — ground (lanes, background, headers), then nodes (cards, text, badges), then connectors (arrows and decision links) — with a short result returned after each phase [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:82] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:84]. This sits between Flow Mode's single hosted call and iteration 4's one-node canary: it is a per-layer checkpoint, not a per-node one.

Per-call node limits are explicit and time-based: 1–6 `shapeWithText` nodes fit the default 5000ms, 7–12 need `timeout: 10000`, and 13+ must be split across calls [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:150] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:152]. Flow Mode's 9-node cap falls inside the 7–12 band, so the cap already implies a non-default timeout on this route [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:43]; Flow Mode's `fj` route states no timeout at all.

The font failure is named precisely: `createShapeWithText()` defaults to **Inter Medium**, and loading Inter Regular is not enough — the shape still fails [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:59] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:65]. Iterations 3 and 4 said "load fonts"; this gives the exact style that must be loaded.

The decision diamond is built manually with `createPolygon(pointCount=4)` plus `rotation=45` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:119]. This shows the shape vocabulary is a function of the route's primitives, not a universal design rule, and supports Flow Mode keeping a route-specific four-shape set rather than a global one [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:97].

Retry policy is tiered: a timeout is retried once, then scope is narrowed (fewer nodes, lower depth); an empty response means checking the target node or page; rate limits are checked explicitly [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:171] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:172]. Flow Mode's recovery is ask-then-re-run into a cleared page [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:159], which has no bounded retry count and no scope-reduction step.

Large-file reads start at low scope (`depth=1`, `verbosity="summary"`, screenshots excluded) and only then go node by node [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:99] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:103]. This is the third independent source for bounded read-back, after iteration 2's whole-page warning and iteration 3's `MAX_NODES` cap.

Scan safety is explicit: never scan or return `figma.currentPage.children`; keep only the nodes created in the current step in a local `created[]` list and use that list for zoom [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:90] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/atezer__FMCP/skills/figjam-diagram-builder/SKILL.md:92]. Flow Mode's read-back has no "created nodes only" list, so it cannot distinguish its own output from pre-existing board content — the same problem iteration 2's section rule solves structurally.

The linter is an explicit machine port of the official rules: "Rules come from the official figma-generate-diagram skill and its references", `lint()` returns `{severity, rule, line, message}`, and "Any error means the text must not be sent to Figma" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:3] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:14]. Flow Mode's `flow_check.py` is the only other executable pre-write gate in the corpus [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:6]; everything else is prose, read-back or tool rejection.

A real Mermaid parser check exists but is optional, and when unavailable it must be reported "as not run (never as passed)" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/parsecheck.py:2] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/parsecheck.py:63]. Flow Mode's extractor is hand-written and vendored, so a construct it accepts may still fail the real parser; Flow Mode has no "not run" state at all [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:13].

Density is a split-and-name policy, not only a cap: readability limits are about 25 nodes and 30 edges, oversized diagrams split into `-part-2`, `-part-3`, and "anything left out is named in the diagram's `notes`, never dropped silently" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/references/diagram-types.md:31] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/references/diagram-types.md:32]. Flow Mode splits at 9 nodes but does not require naming what was omitted [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:99].

Unsupported diagram types are skipped with a reason rather than faked [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/references/diagram-types.md:37], matching Flow Mode's honesty rule for unreachable routes [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:131] but applied one level earlier, at request classification.

The reserved-ID check is broader than the official prose: `end`, `subgraph`, `graph` **plus** the Mermaid keywords `style`, `class`, `classdef`, `click`, `default`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `linkstyle` are errors [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:37] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:45] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:523]. This answers Q4's reserved-word half with an implemented list, not an inference.

Underscores are an **error**, with the reason written into the message: "node id ... contains '_' (breaks Figma edge routing)" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:526]. Non-camelCase IDs are only a warning, and subgraph IDs get both checks [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:532] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:539]. The severity split is a usable design: underscores break routing, so they block; case style is cosmetic, so it warns.

Its direction rule accepts `LR`, `TD`, `TB`, `RL` and `BT`, and only requires `LR` for architecture diagrams [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:211] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:213]. This is machine-enforced counterevidence to Flow Mode's TD-only check [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:61]: the corpus's most rigorous linter treats direction as a per-diagram-type choice.

Emoji, literal `\n`, HTML tags, control/invisible characters, unbalanced quotes and backticks are all caught at the line level [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:150] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/lint.py:157]. Flow Mode checks only HTML, newline and markdown marks, and would pass an emoji [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:44].

The sanitizer is the other half of the same policy: `normalize_text` strips HTML, emoji, invisible and control characters, literal escapes and backticks, then collapses whitespace [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/sanitize.py:307] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/sanitize.py:315]. So the project rejects hand-written text and **fixes** generated text. Flow Mode only rejects; adopting sanitize-on-build for labels would turn an emoji failure into a silent, deterministic repair.

IDs are generated deterministically and reserved words are avoided by an allocator that appends a suffix (`end` becomes a legal ID) [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:223] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:263]. Flow Mode leaves node IDs to the author and its templates use short handwritten names, so a reserved word is a preventable authoring error rather than an impossible one [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/flow-templates.md:33].

`id_map(spec)` exposes the spec-id → Mermaid-id mapping "so the Figma driver can verify what was drawn" [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:10] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:365]. Flow Mode's provenance table maps nodes to sources, not model IDs to board node IDs, so its read-back cannot trace a specific board node back to a model node [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/assets/flow-templates.md:109].

Labels are length-capped at 80 characters with an ellipsis, and IDs at 32 with a short hash [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:24] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:25] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/mermaid/build.py:202]. Flow Mode has no label-length limit, only a one-line rule, while the official reference warns long labels stretch shapes awkwardly [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:320].

Mermaid Jam is a local-only FigJam plugin that converts pasted Mermaid and markdown into native sections, shape cards and dynamic connectors [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/README.md:14]. It is a sixth route — a full parser plus renderer — and the only source that takes arbitrary Mermaid as its primary input rather than generating Mermaid internally.

Unsupported Mermaid types — pie, gantt, erDiagram, classDiagram — return explicit diagnostics instead of bad output [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/README.md:44], corroborating iteration 7's skip-with-reason rule as a corpus norm.

Subgraphs are the one construct the corpus cannot agree on: the official reference supports them up to two nesting levels [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/figma__mcp-server-guide/skills/figma-generate-diagram/references/flowchart.md:157], rocket-path recommends them [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/amo-tech-ai__rocket-path-ai/.agents/skills/figma/figjam-diagrams/SKILL.md:152], and Mermaid Jam rejects them outright as unsupported [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:23]. Flow Mode's silence is therefore a gap either way: it should state whether subgraphs are allowed and, if so, cap nesting at two.

Its header diagnostic names all five accepted directions: `flowchart TD` or `graph LR` with direction `TD, TB, BT, LR, or RL` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:113]. This is the fourth independent source treating direction as a per-diagram choice, and the strongest single piece of counterevidence to Flow Mode's TD-only rule [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:61].

Unsupported constructs are rejected with diagnostics rather than silently dropped: class definitions, class assignments, style directives, linkStyle, click callbacks, init directives, icons and images [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:24] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:31]. Flow Mode's accent rule is expressed through exactly `style`, `classDef` and `linkStyle` [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:47], so an accent rule is only meaningful on routes that support styling.

IDs are normalized rather than checked: `sanitizeId` keeps only alphanumeric words, upper-cases each word, joins the first five, and prefixes `Step` when the result does not start with a letter [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:845] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:857]. Underscores cannot survive, and duplicates get a numeric suffix [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:849]. That is a third strategy: ompug suffixes reserved words, Flow Mode relies on author discipline, Mermaid Jam rewrites the ID.

Labels are repaired, not only rejected: the reviser removes filler phrases ("in order to", "that are", "the user") and hard-caps a label at 120 characters with a word-safe ellipsis [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/shared/reviser.ts:133] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/shared/reviser.ts:138]. Compare ompug's 80-character cap and Flow Mode's no cap; all three approaches accept that long labels are a defect.

"Revise" is a repair-then-parse pass: it strips fences, normalizes arrow glyphs to `-->`, adds `flowchart TD` when the header is missing, dedupes statements, quotes labels with special characters, then re-parses and serializes only if the result is valid [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/shared/reviser.ts:66] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/shared/reviser.ts:115]. Flow Mode has no repair pass; a failing model must be edited by hand and re-checked [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:151].

The reviser refuses oversized sources: above 700 lines it returns an error telling the user to split into diagrams under 700 lines [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/shared/reviser.ts:24] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/shared/reviser.ts:28]. This is a pre-work size gate; Flow Mode's equivalent is a post-model node cap, which does not bound the input size that produced it [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/scripts/flow_check.py:43].

Generated output is always contained in a FigJam section [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/README.md:30], and on update it preserves manually moved node positions when IDs match [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/README.md:27] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/plugin/main/renderer.ts:876]. Flow Mode guarantees neither: the hosted route adds a new diagram rather than updating one, and its rollback is a page clear rather than a container-scoped replace [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:117].

Diagnostics are line-numbered and returned before generation, together with a cleaned source; generation is refused when any diagnostic is an error [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:143] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/memi-design__mermaid-jam/src/parser/mermaidJam.ts:144]. This is the third executable pre-write check in the corpus, after Flow Mode and ompug, and it reports diagnostics as data rather than console text.

The driver defines a fixed publish order: confirm, `whoami` for the plan key, then per diagram `generate_diagram` followed by `use_figma place_section`, then legend, deletion of obsolete sections, `get_figjam` verification and `get_screenshot` for mismatches [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:9] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:11]. This is the concrete hybrid sequence Flow Mode's write step describes only as "hosted first, `fj` when not connected" [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:64].

Verification work is bounded: at most 40 expected labels are compared per diagram [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:33]. At Flow Mode's nine-node cap the bound never binds, but it shows the corpus treats read-back as a budgeted operation rather than an unbounded diff.

The FigJam root is addressed as node `0:1`, and the placement script forbids `figma.createPage` and `figma.notify` outright [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:44] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/scripts.py:5]. This is the third independent implementation decision against page-based targeting, after the official warning and iteration 2's API notes.

Section placement is idempotent by content hash: `place_section` returns an existing section already tagged with the same diagram, run and content hash instead of creating a duplicate [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/scripts.py:14] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/scripts.py:16]. Flow Mode's re-run has no idempotency key, which is why it needs user agreement before a second write [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:159].

Every counted action is persisted as `pending_action` **before** it is returned, so a crash leaves an explicitly *uncertain* action that must be reconciled with `get_figjam`, or with a user question when no file exists yet, before any retry [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:5] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:7] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:260]. Flow Mode has no uncertain state: a failed hosted call is indistinguishable from a call that landed.

Deletion is scoped and auditable: only diagrams whose status is `obsolete` and whose `section_id` is known are deleted, in one `remove obsolete sections` action, and a failure is recorded as a warning rather than retried blindly [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:674] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:684]. This is the concrete form of the "delete the nodes the write created" rollback Flow Mode promises but does not operationalize [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:117].

Read-back is quantified: expected labels are extracted from the diagram spec or Mermaid source, and a diagram passes when at least 60% of them appear in its section subtree; missing labels are returned for reporting [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:32] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:1191] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:1371]. Flow Mode's exact "8 of 8" is stricter and better for a nine-node cap; the transferable part is the **missing-label list**, which Flow Mode's read-back sentence cannot express [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:140].

`get_screenshot` is targeted, not routine: it runs for diagrams whose text verification mismatched, or for all diagrams only with `--verify-visual` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:711] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:718]. Flow Mode always asks for a screenshot check on the board, which is safe but costs a visual step even when counts already match [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:65].

Each action declares which official skills must be loaded before it runs — `generate_diagram` needs `figma-generate-diagram`; `use_figma` and both read tools need `figma-use-figjam` [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:29] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/driver.py:39]. This is a second independent implementation of iteration 1's pre-load requirement, applied per tool rather than once.

Sections are named with a stable prefix and supplemented by a legend section, one palette colour per row, with at least 48px padding [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/scripts.py:26] [SOURCE: specs/z-staging-po-009-research/corpus/ompug__diagram-codebase/skills/diagram-codebase/scripts/diagram_codebase/figma/scripts.py:28]. Flow Mode's board has no naming convention and no legend, so a multi-diagram flow is navigable only by position [SOURCE: AI Systems/Product Owner/sk-product-owner/references/flow-mode.md:99].
